title: Sampling-loop probability
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input symbols, let $sp:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and fix a Boolean input $x$. Suppose $N$ uses at most $sp(|y|)$ work-tape cells on every input $y$ and every choice word, $sp(|x|)\le S$, the configuration-code bound for $N$, $|x|$, and $S$ is at most $K$, and $n+\ell+S+2K+2\le B$. Let $i,cnt\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $i\le K+1$ and $cnt+1\le K+1$, and let $A_1,A_0\in\mathbb{Q}$ be such that for every $c,d\le K$, the run-loop configurations with accepting-run counts $cnt+1$ and $cnt$, respectively, have probabilities $A_1$ and $A_0$. Then for every $j\in\mathbb{N}$, every configuration $C$ on input $x$ reachable from the initial configuration in the sense that its machine state, input-head position, work-tape contents and head positions, and output summary agree with those of a configuration reached by some choice word, and every $d\le K$, the sampling-loop configuration initialized with the code of $C$ has probability $\Pr[\text{accepting after }j\text{ random choice bits}]A_1+(1-\Pr[\text{accepting after }j\text{ random choice bits}])A_0$, where the probability is taken over uniformly random choice words of length $j$.

replaced:
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine on a Boolean input $x$, and
let $sp$ bound its space usage on every input and every choice word. Suppose $sp(|x|)\le
S$, the configuration-code bound for $N,|x|,S$ is at most $K$, and $n+\ell+S+2K+2\le B$.
Let $i,cnt\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $i\le K+1$ and $cnt+1\le K+1$, and let
$A_1,A_0\in\mathbb Q$ be such that, for all $c,d\le K$, the run-loop amplifier
configurations with accepting-run count $cnt+1$ and $cnt$, respectively, have
probabilities $A_1$ and $A_0$. Then for every $j\in\mathbb N$, machine configuration $C$
on $x$, and $d\in\mathbb N$ with $j\le K$, $C$ reachable from the initial configuration
by some choice word (up to its core state, head positions, and summarized output), and
$d\le K$, the amplifier at its sampling-loop label with registers initialized using the
code of $C$ has probability $\Pr[\text{accept after }j\text{ random
choices}]A_1+(1-\Pr[\text{accept after }j\text{ random choices}])A_0$.
